title: NY State Senate · District 19
area: Southeast Brooklyn (Canarsie, East New York, Brownsville) and parts of Lindenwood and Howard Beach, Queens

context.text: Roxanne Persaud is unopposed on the November 3 general-election ballot. Her Democratic primary, scheduled for June 23, 2026, was canceled because she had no primary opponent.

candidates.name: Roxanne Persaud
candidates.ballotNote: Nominated without a primary opponent; running unopposed in the general election

summary.text: Roxanne Persaud is the incumbent Democratic state senator for District 19 in Brooklyn. Born in Guyana, she worked in higher-education administration and held several community posts before serving in the State Assembly and then winning a 2015 special election for the Senate. She chairs the Senate Social Services Committee and is the only candidate listed on the November 3, 2026 ballot for the seat.

background.text: Born in Guyana, South America, and migrated to the United States with her parents and siblings; she lives in the Canarsie section of the 19th Senatorial District.
Graduated from Pace University, where she earned a Bachelor of Science and a Master of Science in Education Administration.
Before entering the legislature, worked in higher-education administration, according to her official Senate biography.

Served as President of the 69th Precinct Community Council in Canarsie, a member of Community Board 18, and a Commissioner on the New York City Districting Commission; also served on the Community Action Board of the NYC Department of Youth and Community Development and chaired the Neighborhood Advisory Board for District 18.

Her official bio also lists graduation from the NYPD Citizens Police Academy and the NYC Office of Emergency Management's Community Emergency Response Team program, and overseas volunteer work on medical and social outreach programs.
Elected to the State Assembly's 59th District in the November 2014 general election, taking office in 2015.

Won the November 2015 special election for the State Senate's 19th District, defeating Republican Jeffrey J. Ferretti and Conservative Elias J. Weir; the seat was vacant after John L. Sampson was removed from office on July 24, 2015.

Chairs the Senate Social Services Committee in the 2025-2026 session; also sits on the Children and Families, Cities 1, Codes, Disabilities, New York City Education, and Transportation committees, the Joint Senate Task Force on Opioids, Addiction & Overdose Prevention, and the Legislative Women's Caucus.

priorities.text: Safer communities, including legislation to tackle gun violence
Supportive services for youth and seniors
Aiding small businesses and building "a vigorous social service agenda"

positions.summary: In a January 2020 Jim Owles Liberal Democratic Club questionnaire, said she supports the New York Health Act, a single-payer system.
positions.quote: I fully support the New York Health Act, also known as “Medicare for All”

positions.summary: In a 2018 press release, urged passage of the Reproductive Health Act, which would update New York's abortion statutes, and the Comprehensive Contraception Coverage Act.
positions.quote: We must do everything in our power to expand access to the full range of reproductive health services

record.text: Sponsored S9491, providing eligibility for state or local public benefits regardless of immigration status; referred to the Senate Finance Committee as of March 2026.

Sponsored S9084, establishing a two-year maternal health monitoring pilot program with $600,000 in state funding for up to 500 Medicaid recipients; passed the Senate Women's Issues Committee in May 2026 and was referred to Finance.

Secured state budget items for District 19 and statewide social-service programs in the SFY 2026-2027 budget, including added funding for the Nutrition Outreach and Education Program, the Disability Assistance Program, statewide diaper banks, and a $200,000 NYPD Youth Explorer program allocation for the district.
Chairs the Senate Social Services Committee in the 2025-2026 session.
